title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is the first page of an offprint of a published Comptes Rendus note: Marcus Wanderley, 'Théorie axiomatique de l'orientation des variétés topologiques à bord', C. R. Acad. Sc. Paris t. 292 (19 Jan 1981), Série I, p. 213, presented by H. Cartan. It is filed in Grothendieck's folder after a sheet headed 'Orientation', which suggests Wanderley was working in Grothendieck's Montpellier circle; whether formally as his student is unsure.

The mathematics, in modern language:
- **Setting.** N is a positive integer or ∞. 𝒱•_{≤N} is the category of topological manifolds with boundary of dimension ≤ N, with open embeddings as morphisms. 𝒱_{≤N} is the full subcategory of manifolds without boundary. The superscript 0 denotes the opposite category, so functors on it are presheaves.
- **Extension to manifolds with boundary.** A presheaf F on boundaryless manifolds is extended to manifolds with boundary by F•(V) = F(Int V).
- **Data of an orientation theory T = (Ω, δ, ν).**
  1. A contravariant functor Ω : 𝒱_{≤N}^op → Sets, the orientation functor. Ω•(V) is the set of orientations of V.
  2. Natural 'Stokes maps' δ_V : Ω•(V) → Ω(∂V), giving the induced boundary orientation.
  3. A normalization bijection ν : {±1} ≅ Ω(point).
- **Axioms.**
  - (a) Exactness: Ω restricted to the open sets of any V is a sheaf.
  - (b)–(d), on the next page: the sheaf is separated in the sense that the locus where two orientations agree is clopen; δ is a local isomorphism of étalé spaces along ∂V; and an anti-commutativity rule for gluing V = V' ∪ V'' along a common boundary.
- **Consequence and theorem.** The étalé space of Ω over V is a double cover, the orientation cover. Theorem 1 states:
  - existence of an orientation theory;
  - morphisms between theories are unique and are isomorphisms;
  - for N ≠ 4, any two theories are isomorphic.
- **Role of Kirby.** The proof uses Kirby's theorem that every degree +1 homeomorphism of R^n is stable when n ≠ 4. A stable homeomorphism is a composite of homeomorphisms each equal to the identity on some open set. By the sheaf property and connectedness, such a homeomorphism acts trivially on Ω(R^n). This makes Ω determined by its local behaviour, which forces it to agree with the standard (local-homology) orientation theory.
- **Purpose.** This is an axiomatic, sheaf-theoretic uniqueness theorem for orientations, in the style of Eilenberg–Steenrod. It is very much in the Grothendieck spirit of characterizing a structure by functoriality and local axioms. The folder context (Gauss–Manin, Cartier) suggests Grothendieck kept it as a reference on sign and orientation conventions, e.g. for Stokes-type boundary maps.
errors: 'unduite' in the definition of the Stokes map is a misprint in the original for 'induite'.

The restriction N ≠ 4 reflects the state of knowledge in 1981. Quinn (1982, 'Ends of maps III') proved the 4-dimensional annulus/stable homeomorphism theorem, which should allow part (c) to hold for all N. This consequence is not stated here because it postdates the note.
No mathematical error is visible on this page; it contains definitions only.

ideas.what: Axiomatic definition of an orientation theory: a sheaf Ω on the site of manifolds with open embeddings, with Stokes boundary maps and a normalization at a point, satisfying separation, local-isomorphism and anti-commutativity axioms
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic characterization of the orientation double cover / orientation local system (Eilenberg–Steenrod-style uniqueness)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Marcus Wanderley (CRAS 1981); orientation via local homology is classical (Seifert–Threlfall, Steenrod)
ideas.where_published: Wanderley, C. R. Acad. Sc. Paris 292 (1981), Série I, pp. 213–214

ideas.what: Extension of presheaves from manifolds to manifolds with boundary via the interior, F•(V) = F(Int V)
Uniqueness of orientation theory via Kirby's stable homeomorphism theorem (degree +1 homeomorphisms of R^n act trivially on any such sheaf)
ideas.modern_name: Stable homeomorphism theorem applied to the rigidity of natural local systems on Top-manifolds
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kirby 1969 (SH for n ≥ 5), Quinn 1982 (n = 4); the application is Wanderley 1981

missed.claim: The N ≠ 4 hypothesis in Wanderley's uniqueness theorem appears removable using Quinn's 1982 proof of the stable homeomorphism theorem in dimension 4. That would make the theory unique in all dimensions. I am unsure whether this was ever recorded.
missed.quote: on prouve l'unicité (à isomorphisme près) d'une telle théorie lorsque N≠4, en s'appuyant sur un résultat de Kirby
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor completion of a published result. It is a small historical note rather than new mathematics.

missed.claim: The presence of this offprint in Grothendieck's Gauss–Manin/Cartier folder, after a sheet titled 'Orientation', documents his interest in, and likely supervision of or influence on, Wanderley's axiomatic orientation theory. This link is little noted.
missed.quote: Note (*) de Marcus Wanderley, présentée par Henri Cartan
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for mapping Grothendieck's Montpellier students and their topics.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a published CRAS offprint by another author, not a Grothendieck manuscript. Its interest is historical (Grothendieck's Montpellier circle) plus the small observation that Quinn's 1982 work removes the N ≠ 4 restriction.
transcription_corrections: 'unduite' is faithful to the printed text, which itself has a misprint for 'induite'.
The superscript '0' on the categories denotes the opposite category (presheaves), not dimension 0.
The handwritten '27' at bottom left is the archive page number.
